briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. Let's begin the climate briefing for July 31, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Worst-Ever Heatwave and Drought Spreading as a Global Threat
sections.content: Domestically today, the daytime temperature in Yangsan, Gyeongnam, soared to 41.4 degrees Celsius, breaking the all-time record since meteorological observations began, and a severe heatwave warning has been in effect for a week across the Gyeongnam region [101, 105, 106]. This extreme heatwave and drought are causing severe problems such as drinking water shortages, crop damage, and high sea surface temperatures, with over 1,700 heat-related illness patients reported nationwide and an estimated 13 deaths [102, 103, 107]. In Europe, too, heatwaves and droughts have lowered water levels in major waterways like the Danube River to their lowest in 30 years, leading to the suspension of nuclear power plant operations and triggering an energy security alert [5, 10, 11, 152]. The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned about the health impacts of such extreme heat due to climate change, emphasizing the need to recognize heatwaves not merely as weather phenomena but as social disasters, and advocating for a human-centric response [12, 17, 20, 123].

sections.title: ⚠️ Wildfire Risk Due to Climate Change Strikes Europe and North America
sections.content: International researchers have analyzed that climate change is the cause of the large-scale wildfires in France and Spain, leading to at least a 20-fold increase in the likelihood of such fires [2, 108, 109, 116, 117, 120, 130, 131, 132, 151]. Across Europe, warnings continue that climate change is creating 'tinderbox conditions' for wildfires and making large-scale wildfires more common [110, 118, 121, 122, 124, 127, 133, 135, 136, 138, 139, 140, 141, 145, 147, 148, 149, 150, 154]. Particularly in France and Spain, destructive wildfires are ongoing [112, 148, 149], and North America is also directly hit by climate change, with over 150 wildfires breaking out in northwestern Ontario, Canada, leading to the evacuation of more than 1,800 residents [153].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Companies and Local Governments Accelerate Carbon Neutrality Implementation
sections.content: Domestic companies are taking proactive steps to achieve their carbon neutrality goals. Hanmi Group has introduced Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) for renewable energy and launched a roadmap, targeting RE100 and carbon neutrality by 2040 [26, 33, 43, 44, 55, 57, 59, 66, 71, 72, 73, 79, 81, 82, 85, 89], while SK Eternix and Hyundai Engineering & Construction have also unveiled their carbon neutrality roadmaps for 2040 and 2045, respectively [31, 39, 63, 69, 99]. Lotte Group strengthened its ESG management by exceeding its carbon emission reduction target by 3.8% last year [25, 32, 42, 49, 51]. Furthermore, NH Nonghyup Bank issued 100 billion won worth of Korean-style green bonds to support carbon neutrality [56, 61, 62], and Korea Zinc Chairman Choi Yun-beom proposed that Korea and Chile create a critical minerals cooperation model to lead carbon neutrality [24, 35, 40, 48, 64].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Community Climate Crisis Adaptation and Renewable Energy Infrastructure Development
sections.content: Domestic local governments are making concrete efforts to prepare for climate change and achieve carbon neutrality. Muju County is laying the groundwork for future agriculture by installing plant factories in preparation for climate change [3, 14], while Michuhol District and Bucheon City have begun developing customized climate crisis adaptation measures, discussing solutions with experts and residents [15, 16, 23]. Jeju Province has achieved the nation's first residential heating electrification project, signaling the start of household carbon neutrality [54], and Chungju City is contributing to reducing carbon emissions in public transportation by introducing additional eco-friendly hydrogen buses [58]. Meanwhile, the National Assembly is promoting the introduction of a renewable energy contract market and the reorganization of the RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) system, establishing an institutional foundation for expanding renewable energy. However, caution is also required regarding grid risks associated with the rapid acceleration of renewable energy [74, 88].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing. We kindly request your continued interest and efforts in addressing climate change.
